output.summary: The record year tracks the February-June 2026 commodity rally, not operations: grain sales were 91% of revenue, handling revenue was flat ($9.8M to $9.9M) while bushels fell, and peers' median revenue growth was +41%. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes entirely from maintenance, which fell as deferred work orders tripled to $1.26M; non-maintenance cost was flat. Safety evidence is serious: insurer critical findings at Harlan Junction, a near-miss with an overheated bearing after a repeatedly deferred work order, and an unclosed SP-04 investigation. Drying knowledge sits with one nearing-retirement superintendent with no successor. The expansion case is unestablished: no pro forma, unsourced throughput, and revenue baselined on rally-inflated FY2026 figures. Fix the hazards and start succession now; defer the vote.
